Heritage walk · Puducherry

Heritage walk in Puducherry: the French and Tamil quarters and Arikamedu

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Puducherry (Pondicherry) covers the planned grid of the former French capital in India: White Town by the sea, with its villas, churches and the promenade, and the Tamil quarter west of the old canal, with its verandah houses and temples. Arikamedu, an Indo-Roman trading site of the early centuries CE, lies about 4 km south.

We arrange Puducherry heritage walks on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, led by an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, with other languages through partners.

Why Puducherry matters for heritage

Puducherry was the headquarters of French possessions in India from the late 17th century until 1954, when it was transferred to India (the formal treaty came into force in 1962). Its town plan, a grid split by a canal into a European quarter by the sea and a Tamil quarter inland, survives better than almost any colonial plan in the country. So does a distinctive local architecture that mixes French classical facades with Tamil verandahs and courtyards.

Long before the French, the coast here was part of Indian Ocean trade. Arikamedu, excavated by Mortimer Wheeler in 1945 and by later teams, produced Roman amphorae, Arretine ware and beads, evidence of contact with the Mediterranean in roughly the 1st century BCE to the 2nd century CE. Our lecture on foods as historical evidence explains what that trade carried.

Historical places in Puducherry by period

The French East India Company took Pondichéry in 1674. The Dutch held it between 1693 and 1699, and the British captured it several times in the 18th century wars, destroying much of the town in 1761. Most of what you see was rebuilt after that, on the original grid, by the late 18th and 19th centuries.

Key layers include the Manakula Vinayagar Temple, older than the French town in tradition; the Jesuit Church of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception (present building completed 1791); the Basilica of the Sacred Heart (1908); and the 20th century arrival of Sri Aurobindo, whose ashram from 1926 shaped part of White Town.

Places a heritage walk in Puducherry covers

  1. Goubert Avenue promenade French town plan

    The seafront road of White Town. Start here to understand the grid running back from the sea.

  2. Old Lighthouse 1836

    Early lighthouse on the promenade, now disused, beside the old port.

  3. Gandhi statue and pillars Statue 20th century, pillars older

    The statue stands among carved stone pillars that local accounts say were brought from Gingee.

  4. French War Memorial 1938

    Memorial to soldiers from Pondichéry who died in the First World War.

  5. Bharathi Park 18th to 19th century

    The central square of White Town, with the Aayi Mandapam monument at its centre.

  6. Raj Niwas 18th century origins

    Former residence of the French governors, now the Lieutenant Governor's residence. Seen from outside.

  7. Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Completed 1791

    Jesuit cathedral on a site used for churches since the late 17th century.

  8. Manakula Vinayagar Temple Tradition older than the French town

    Ganesha temple in White Town, a reminder that the town grew around existing shrines.

  9. Tamil quarter streets 18th to 20th century

    Houses with thinnai verandahs and courtyards, west of the old canal. Look at doorways and pillars.

  10. Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus 1908

    Gothic-style church with stained glass, near the railway station.

  11. Pondicherry Museum Collection 20th century

    Arikamedu finds, bronzes and French period objects.

  12. Arikamedu About 1st century BCE to 2nd century CE

    Indo-Roman trading site on the Ariyankuppam river, about 4 km south. Vehicle needed.

Museums in Puducherry

  • Pondicherry Museum. Arikamedu pottery and beads, bronzes, French period objects.
  • Bharathi Memorial Museum. The house where Subramania Bharati lived in exile.
  • Bharathidasan Memorial Museum. Home of the Tamil poet Bharathidasan, with manuscripts and photographs.

Best time for a walk

December to February. October and November bring heavy northeast monsoon rain; summers are humid.

What you see on a heritage walk in Puducherry

In White Town the walk follows the beach road (Goubert Avenue) past the old lighthouse, the Gandhi statue on a plinth of pillars that are said to come from Gingee, the French War Memorial and the Hôtel de Ville. Behind them, Rue Romain Rolland and the streets around Bharathi Park show the high walls, gateways and shuttered windows of French villas, with Raj Niwas, the Lieutenant Governor's residence, facing the park.

Across the canal, the Tamil quarter has a different rhythm: houses with a thinnai (raised verandah) facing the street, a courtyard inside, and Madras terrace roofs. INTACH and local residents have worked to document and conserve these streets. The heritage photography walk suits this area, where details such as doorways and pillars tell the story.

Museums in Puducherry

The Pondicherry Museum near Bharathi Park displays Arikamedu finds, Chola bronzes, French period furniture and coins. The house of the Tamil poet Subramania Bharati, who lived here in exile from 1908 to 1918, is now a small museum. A museum gallery study with an archaeologist works well with the Arikamedu material.

Puducherry heritage walk for schools and colleges

Puducherry is flat, shaded in parts and quiet in the early morning, which makes it easy for school groups. The walk links to European trading companies, the Carnatic wars and the freedom movement. Architecture and planning students can study the grid, the canal and the conservation regulations; history students can trace Indo-Roman trade at Arikamedu.

Puducherry walks are shaped around your group and the time you have. Groups often combine the city with Mahabalipuram and Gingee; see our Mamallapuram programme and the south India temple architecture study tour.

Practical advice for groups

Walk early: by 10 am the sea road fills and the sun is strong. The beach road is closed to traffic in the evenings. Churches and temples have their own rules; the Aurobindo Ashram has fixed visiting hours and asks for silence. Arikamedu is an open site with little to see above ground, so prepare students with the museum first. Check the site or museum website before you go, and see heritage sites in Puducherry for Karaikal and other enclaves.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Puducherry?

The promenade, Old Lighthouse, Bharathi Park, Raj Niwas, the Immaculate Conception Cathedral, the Sacred Heart Basilica, the Manakula Vinayagar Temple, the Tamil quarter, the Pondicherry Museum and the Arikamedu site.

What is Arikamedu?

An early historic port near Puducherry where excavations found Roman amphorae, Mediterranean pottery and beads, evidence of trade with the Roman world around the 1st century BCE to the 2nd century CE.

When did Puducherry become part of India?

De facto transfer from France took place on 1 November 1954. The treaty of cession was ratified and came into force in 1962.

Is a Puducherry heritage walk good for school groups?

Yes. White Town is flat and compact, and the walk links to European trading companies and the Carnatic wars. Start early to avoid heat and traffic.
